author: duncan4123
body:
## Summary
- expose session workdirs/titles through `gc session list` and the session API for packrouter lookup
- propagate trigger bead metadata into pool-backed session desired state and pre_start context
- route pack pool sessions into reusable per-pack workspaces by default
- keep named/task workspaces available through explicit bead metadata
- add lint/test coverage for invalid named-session/pool-control combinations and trigger-driven pool demand

## Related Gas City work
- #3582 fixes named-session workdir precedence: configured named-session workdirs win over stale session metadata, while task-specific workdirs still win when a task intentionally supplies one.
- This PR builds on that split: named sessions stay configured/stable, while pool workers can be rebound to trigger-specific task metadata and pack workdirs.

## Related pack changes
- [packer pack](https://github.com/duncan4123/gascity-packs/tree/7812550575a0668196592c62204b04243f1a1512/packer): owns the bead-creation workflow. By default it creates pack-routed beads that reuse the pack workspace. `--workspace <name>` targets a named workspace, and `--task-workspace` creates a workspace key from the child bead id/title. It now includes `packer/assets/scripts/list-pack-workspaces.sh`, which lets packrouter inspect existing packsmith workspaces before creating child beads.
- [jjw pack](https://github.com/duncan4123/gascity-packs/tree/a949f8e8affe8eb33cda321492cb044256c507df/jjw): provides the jj workspace creation layer used by packer and serializes setup so concurrent pack work does not race while rewriting the shared jjw config and creating workspaces.

## How it works
Pack-routed work beads carry the pack route in metadata such as `gc.pack` and `gc.pack_root`. When those beads create demand for a pool-backed agent, desired-state keeps the demand tied to the individual triggering work bead instead of treating the pool as one generic agent slot.

The selected pool session gets durable trigger metadata on its session bead: `gc.trigger_bead_id`, `gc.trigger_bead_store_ref`, the pack route fields, and the derived `work_dir`. If `gc.pack` is set and `gc.pack_workspace` is absent, the derived workdir is the reusable pack workspace: `.gc/workspaces/<rig>/packs/<pack>`. If `gc.pack_workspace` is set, the derived workdir is `.gc/workspaces/<rig>/packs/<pack>/<workspace>`.

At runtime start/resume, that durable metadata is converted into pre_start environment variables: `GC_TRIGGER_BEAD_ID`, `GC_TRIGGER_WORK_BEAD_ID`, `GC_TRIGGER_BEAD_STORE_REF`, `GC_TRIGGER_WORK_STORE_REF`, and `GC_PACKER_PACK`. The packer pack's pre_start script consumes those values, reads the trigger bead from the correct rig store, chooses the pack root, and delegates to the jjw workspace setup. That gives the agent a workspace matching the bead it was actually routed to.

Packrouter now has an explicit lookup step for follow-up routing. `packer/assets/scripts/list-pack-workspaces.sh --pack <pack>` reads `gc session list --json --state all`, parses packsmith `work_dir` values, and shows the session target plus title, so the router can reuse the default pack workspace or a named workspace without a human manually inspecting session rows.

## Named sessions
Named sessions keep their stable configured identity and configured workdir semantics from #3582. They are not expanded into one session per trigger bead, and they should not be used as the durable identity for pool-controlled pack work. This PR adds lint coverage for the bad configuration where a named session is backed by a pool-controlled agent, because that shape has one stable name but needs multiple trigger-specific routing contexts.

If a session bead already has trigger metadata, the runtime config can still receive the `GC_TRIGGER_*` env on start/resume. The important behavior is that named-session identity remains name-based and configuration-driven, while trigger-specific routing belongs to pool worker sessions whose durable session bead can be rebound to the selected work bead.

## Pool workers
Pool workers keep their normal worker names, such as `packer.packsmith-2`, but the session bead records which work bead that worker is serving. Desired-state carries the assigned work bead id, title, store ref, pack, and optional workspace key through pool demand selection. When a worker is created or selected, Gas City binds that trigger data to the session bead and updates `work_dir` to the pack workspace or explicit named workspace.

That lets multiple workers from the same pool serve different packs at the same time. For example, one `packer.packsmith-*` worker can be bound to a `jj-hunk` task while another is bound to a `jjw` or `packer` task, even though they all use the same pool template. Follow-up work can reuse the same pack workspace by default; task-specific isolation is requested by bead creation using `gc.pack_workspace`.

## Resume behavior
Resume uses the session bead as the source of truth, not the agent name, current shell cwd, or the current jj bookmark. On start/resume, Gas City reloads the session bead metadata, rebuilds the trigger env from it, and runs pre_start with those values. If the same worker resumes the same trigger bead, it returns to the same derived workdir. If desired-state rebinds an asleep pool worker to a different work bead, the trigger metadata and `work_dir` are updated before the next runtime start so pre_start re-enters the correct pack or named workspace.

The store ref is part of the persisted metadata so pack scripts can load the trigger bead from the right bead store (`city` vs `rig:<name>`) during resume. That is what lets packer recover the actual pack route even after the original dispatch context is gone.

## Tests
- `go test ./cmd/gc -run 'TestRealizePoolDesiredSessions(HonorsExplicitPackWorkspace|RebindUpdatesPackWorkspaceMetadata|BindsTriggerBeadToFreshSession)|TestDefaultScaleCheckDemandCarriesTriggerBeadID' -count=1 -timeout 60s`
- `pytest -q packer/tests/test_packer_pack.py` on the packer pack change
- Real smoke test: created existing jj workspace `route-smoke-20260620-150307`, created/slung `gp-gau` with `gc.pack_workspace=route-smoke-20260620-150307`, observed `dg-wisp-09cgn` bind to `.gc/workspaces/gascity-packs/packs/packer/route-smoke-20260620-150307`, then closed the smoke bead. This exposed and fixed stale `gc.pack_workspace` / `gc.work_dir` metadata on pool-session rebind.
- `sh -n packer/assets/scripts/create-pack-bead.sh packer/assets/scripts/pack-workspace-setup.sh`
- `sh -n jjw/assets/scripts/workspace-setup.sh` on the jjw pack change




## Test
- go test ./cmd/gc -run 'Test(RenderSessionListFromAPI|CmdSessionList_RendersLastNudgeColumn|RouteSessionList_APIJSONIncludesCacheAge)' -count=1 -timeout 90s
- go test ./internal/api -run 'TestSessionsFromGenList' -count=1 -timeout 90s
- python3 -m pytest packer/tests/test_packer_pack.py -q
- gc lint packer
- make dashboard-check
- go vet ./...
title: Route pack pool sessions from trigger beads
